NLRP3_inflammasome -> inflammation.validation_notes: Well-established mechanistic and clinical support; IL-1 blockade meta-analysis (n=2921) shows significant HbA1c reduction.

hydroxychloroquine -> T2D.validation_notes: Meta-analysis of 11 RCTs (n=2723) shows HbA1c reduction -0.88 to -1.35% vs placebo; improves beta cell function and lipids.

metformin -> T2D.validation_notes: Multiple systematic reviews/meta-analyses confirm HbA1c reduction ~0.95-1.32% vs placebo; reduces T2D incidence ~23-25% in high-risk adults.

oxidative_stress -> inflammation.validation_notes: Recent systematic reviews/meta-analyses confirm oxidative stress as major inflammation driver in diabetes (291 SR/MA results in PubMed).

dapagliflozin -> T2D.validation_notes: SGLT2i dapagliflozin extensively validated for T2D — 260 RCT/meta-analyses in PubMed. Well-established. || Phase 3 trials and multiple meta-analyses confirm HbA1c reduction (~-0.5 to -0.6% monotherapy WMD; -0.53% as combo). FDA approved; first generic approved 2026-04-07.

dapagliflozin -> inflammation.evidence_summary: Multiple RCTs and mechanistic studies confirm dapagliflozin reduces NLRP3 inflammasome activation, lowers IL-1β/IL-6/TNF-α. Nature Comms 2020 (PMID 32332732) shows SGLT2i modulates NLRP3 via ketones. Springer 2017 shows dapagliflozin reduces NLRP3/ASC/caspase-1 in diabetic cardiomyopathy mice.

verapamil -> T1D.validation_notes: April 2026 re-validation: (1) 2018 Ovalle RCT (PMID 29988125) positive for C-peptide AUC preservation at 3/12mo; (2) 2023 Forlenza pediatric RCT positive for C-peptide preservation; (3) 2023 meta-analysis (PMC10424102) across adult+ped RCTs (112 pts) showed significant 1-yr C-peptide benefit; (4) 2025 Ver-A-T1D European multicentre RCT (n=136) — primary endpoint (2h MMTT C-peptide AUC at 12mo) MISSED statistical significance; trend favored verapamil; results presented EASD Sep 2025; Ver-A-Long OL extension ongoing to 24-36mo; (5) 2026 systematic review PMID 40111679 (Cardiovascular Drugs and Therapy) concluded verapamil is safe adjunct with glycemic-control signal but flagged limited scale/heterogeneity. Net interpretation: benefit signal is real but effect size is modest and heterogeneous across trials; the largest/most-recent RCT did NOT confirm primary endpoint. Confidence DOWNGRADED from HIGH to MEDIUM. Do not over-state beta-cell preservation claim.

verapamil -> beta_cell.evidence_summary: Mixed evidence: 2018 Ovalle/Shalev Nat Med RCT positive (PMID 29988125); 2023 Forlenza pediatric RCT positive; 2023 meta-analysis of RCTs (PMC10424102) positive for 1-yr C-peptide benefit. 2025 Ver-A-T1D (European multicentre RCT, n=136, results at EASD 2025) — primary MMTT C-peptide AUC endpoint did NOT reach significance at 3/6/9/12mo (numerical trend favored verapamil). 2026 systematic review PMID 40111679 confirms safety and a glycemic-control signal but cautions about scale/heterogeneity. Preclinical mechanism (TXNIP suppression, β-cell mitochondrial respiration) remains intact. Confidence MEDIUM: evidence of biological signal but an adequately powered contemporary multicentre RCT did not confirm the primary endpoint.

NF_kB -> inflammation.evidence_summary: NF-κB is a well-established master regulator of inflammatory responses in diabetes. Multiple reviews confirm: Frontiers Pharmacology 2017 (PMC5681994), Cell Metab 2011 (PMC3040418). Salicylate/IKKβ inhibition improves glucose tolerance in T2D patients. Curcumin modulates NF-κB to reduce oxidative stress in diabetes (Zamanian 2024).

empagliflozin -> inflammation.evidence_summary: EMPA-CARD RCT showed empagliflozin reduced IL-6 (-1.06 pg/mL, p=0.006) and hs-CRP (-2.86 mg/L, p=0.003) vs placebo. 12-month trial showed 54% hs-CRP reduction. Meta-analysis confirms CRP reduction -0.63 mg/L (p=0.01) and IL-6 SMD -0.28 (p=0.03). EMPA-REG OUTCOME supports cardiovascular benefits partly via anti-inflammatory effects.

dapagliflozin -> nephropathy.validation_notes: DAPA-CKD landmark RCT (NEJM 2020 PMID 32970396, n=4304): dapagliflozin 10 mg vs placebo over median 2.4 y reduced composite (sustained ≥50% eGFR decline, ESKD, renal or CV death) HR 0.61 (95% CI 0.51-0.72). Confirmed by 2024 SR/MA (PMC11370938, 9 RCTs, ~30k participants) showing OR 0.61 (0.57-0.65) for primary kidney composite and OR 0.69 (0.63-0.76) for mortality, with UACR reduction of -23.99% (95% CI -34.82 to -13.15). Effect present in patients with and without T2D. Mechanism strongly supported.

pioglitazone -> T2D.validation_notes: PROactive RCT n=5238 (PMC2291341): 16% reduction in composite MACE; insulin progression halved. Meta-analyses (Nat Sci Rep 2019, PLOS One PMC2701605) confirm glycemic efficacy with weight gain & edema caveats. Caveat: pioglitazone HbA1c effect as monotherapy is comparable to comparators (not superior) but FPG improved.

dorzagliatin -> T2D.validation_notes: SEED phase 3 (PMID 35551294, Nat Med 2022): drug-naive T2D n=463, HbA1c -1.07% vs -0.50% placebo at 24wk. DAWN phase 3 (PMC9117147): add-on to metformin n=767, HbA1c -1.02% vs -0.36%. Both no severe hypoglycemia/drug-related SAEs.

metformin -> nephropathy.validation_notes: 2024 J Clin Endocrinol Metab (PMID 38986038) and 2015 Annals Int Med systematic review (PMID 25536258) show metformin associated with lower incidence of doubling serum creatinine, eGFR ≤15, and ESKD in T2D. Combination with SGLT2i further reduces composite kidney outcomes. NOTE: PARTIALLY_VALIDATED because effect derives largely from observational and cohort data; no dedicated RCT for nephropathy as primary endpoint (vs. SGLT2i which have CKD-primary RCTs). Cross-validated 2026-05-12.

vitamin_d -> autoimmune.validation_notes: PARTIALLY_VALIDATED. Observational meta-analysis (Zipitis & Akobeng 2008; Dong 2013 Nutrients PMID 24036529) suggests early-life vitamin D supplementation reduces T1D risk (OR ~0.71). ABIS study (PMID 17341286) found no protective effect on islet autoimmunity in unselected infants. 2025 Frontiers immunology meta-analysis indicates modest reductions in autoimmunity with supplementation in at-risk children. No prevention RCT has shown definitive T1D incidence reduction. Mechanistic plausibility (VDR on immune cells, regulatory T-cell modulation) is solid. Cross-validated 2026-05-12.

metformin -> cardiovascular.validation_notes: UKPDS 34 (Lancet 1998, PMID 9742976): metformin in overweight T2D reduced all-cause mortality 36% and diabetes-related death 42%. Griffin 2017 Diabetologia meta-analysis (PMID 28770324, 13 RCTs n~4,158): all CV effect sizes favor metformin but none statistically significant (all-cause RR 0.96, MI RR 0.89, CV death RR 0.97). Boussageon 2012 PLoS Med (PMID 22473097) similarly equivocal. PARTIALLY_VALIDATED: foundational UKPDS evidence + biological plausibility, but updated RCT-level meta-analyses do not show consistent significant CV benefit; observational data favorable. Cross-validated 2026-05-12.

tacrolimus -> inflammation.notes: Tacrolimus inhibits NF-kB / NFAT in T cells (PMID 23573283 PLOS One) suppressing TNFa/IL-6/IL-1 -- canonical anti-inflammatory effect. BUT cell-type dependent: PMID 27291296 (Sci Rep) shows TAC induces vascular inflammation via TLR4. PMID 23958496 shows TAC activates NF-kB in tubular cells via JAK2/JNK/TLR4. Net effect: anti-inflammatory in T cells, pro-inflammatory in vascular/renal tissue. Cannot be summarized as simple anti-inflammatory. | PMID AUDIT 2026-05-13: Verified: 23573283 (Maguire 2013 PLOS One: TAC inhibits NF-kB in T cells), 23958496 (Gonzalez-Guerrero 2013: CNIs activate NF-kB in tubular cells via JAK2/JNK/TLR4). Effect is cell-type dependent.

calcineurin -> islet_transplant.notes: Calcineurin inhibitors (tacrolimus, cyclosporine) are diabetogenic and beta-cell toxic. PMID 25255841 (Drug Metab Toxicol 2014) review: CNIs reduce insulin secretion, transcription, induce apoptosis; impair Ca++ flux. PMID 17176613: CNI substitution with MMF resolved beta-cell toxicity in islet recipient. PMID 37359825 (Posselt 2023, Transpl Int): calcineurin-SPARING regimen maintains long-term insulin independence. Validated direction: CNIs HARM islet grafts; field is moving to calcineurin-sparing protocols. | PMID AUDIT 2026-05-13: Verified: 17176613 (CNI substitution resolves beta-cell tox), 25255841 (Tacrolimus pancreas Tx review), 37359825 (Posselt 2023 calcineurin-sparing).

atorvastatin -> T2D.notes: Sattar 2010 (PMID 19794004) IPD meta of 13 trials, 91,140 pts: statins +9% incident T2D. Navarese 2016 NMA (PMID 27277934): atorvastatin specifically +12%, pravastatin neutral/protective. CTT 2024 Lancet D&E IPD meta: confirmed dose-dependent. CV benefits outweigh diabetogenic risk. Path direction: atorvastatin INCREASES T2D risk (not therapeutic). Flag for direction reversal in corpus. | PMID AUDIT 2026-05-13: Verified PMIDs: 19794004 (Sattar 2010 Lancet collaborative meta), 27277934 (Navarese 2016 NMA). Statins +9% T2D risk; atorvastatin specifically +12% in NMA. CV benefits outweigh diabetogenic risk per CTT IPD meta (Lancet D&E 2024, PMID pending verification). Path direction: atorvastatin INCREASES T2D risk (not therapeutic for T2D). Should consider flagging path-direction for review.

belatacept -> T1D.notes: Belatacept (LEA29Y, CTLA-4-Ig) used as calcineurin-sparing maintenance in islet transplant for T1D. PMID 37359825 (Posselt 2023 Transpl Int): 3/5 belatacept patients insulin-independent at 10y, HbA1c 7.1->5.8%. Limited to small CIT-04/08 cohort. Not a primary T1D therapy outside transplant. Mechanism plausible (CD28-B7 blockade) but no large RCT. | PMID AUDIT 2026-05-13: Verified: 37359825 (Posselt 2023 Transpl Int).

belatacept -> islet_transplant.notes: PMID 37359825 (Posselt 2023): belatacept-based calcineurin-sparing immunosuppression maintains long-term insulin independence in islet transplant. CIT-04/08 cohort. Better beta-cell preservation than CNI-based regimens. Validated. | PMID AUDIT 2026-05-13: Verified: 37359825.

rapamycin -> islet_transplant.notes: Sirolimus is core component of Edmonton protocol (PMID 16968130 NEJM 2006 international trial). 5-yr insulin independence dropped to ~10%. Berney 2009 (PMID 18713146 Transpl Int): "friend or foe?" review of dual mechanisms. Sirolimus impairs GSIS, depletes ER Ca++, may reduce engraftment. Mixed evidence: needed for immunosuppression but has direct beta-cell toxicity. PARTIALLY_VALIDATED. | PMID AUDIT 2026-05-13: Verified: 18713146 (Berney 2009 friend-or-foe review). Edmonton NEJM 2006 international trial cited in search but PMID needs separate verification before recording.

rapamycin -> nephropathy.notes: Preclinical evidence robust: PMID 16597691 (Lloberas 2006 JASN): rapamycin slows DKD progression in rats; PMID 16364254 (Sakaguchi 2006 KI): attenuates renal hypertrophy via p70S6K. PMID 27338360 (Lieberthal 2016): mTOR pathway central to DKD. BUT clinical translation limited; in transplant setting, sirolimus + CNI may worsen pre-existing DKD per Shapiro CITR. PARTIALLY_VALIDATED -- preclinical strong, clinical mixed. | PMID AUDIT 2026-05-13: Verified: 16597691 (Lloberas JASN 2006), 16364254 (Sakaguchi 2006 KI), 27338360 (Lieberthal 2016).

empagliflozin -> nephropathy.validation_notes: EMPA-KIDNEY (Herrington et al. NEJM 2023, PMID 36331190): RCT n=6,609 CKD patients, empagliflozin 10mg/d, primary composite (kidney progression or CV death) HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.64-0.82, p<0.000001); 28% relative risk reduction confirmed across eGFR strata. Effect persisted post-trial. Validated via 2026-05-12 web search.

canagliflozin -> inflammation.validation_notes: CANVAS post-hoc mediation analysis (Sen et al. Diabetes Obes Metab 2022, PMID 35635326): canagliflozin in T2D reduced urinary KIM-1, TNFR-1, TNFR-2 and MCP-1; reduction in tubular inflammation partly mediated benefit. CANVAS primary publication (Neal et al. NEJM 2017, PMID 28605608) provides core trial context. SGLT2i class systematic review (23 studies, n=1,654) shows hsCRP reduction independent of HbA1c. VALIDATED. Cross-validated 2026-05-12.

NLRP3_inflammasome -> T2D.notes: Strongly validated mechanistic link. PMID 34536551 (Karasawa 2021 Cardiovasc Res) reviews NLRP3 in T2D/atherosclerosis. PMID 17554302 (Larsen NEJM 2007): anakinra (IL-1RA) improved beta-cell function in T2D in 13-wk RCT -- proof of concept for IL-1beta pathway. NLRP3-IL-1beta-IRS axis disrupts insulin signaling. Donath group ongoing T2D inflammasome trials. Mechanism: obesity activates NLRP3 in adipose macrophages -> IL-1beta -> IRS serine phosphorylation -> insulin resistance. | PMID AUDIT 2026-05-13: Verified: 34536551 (Karasawa 2021 review). Anakinra NEJM 2007 (Larsen) cited but PMID not directly confirmed in search; mechanistic link well-supported by multiple reviews.

Treg_expansion -> T1D.validation_notes: T-Rex phase 2 RCT (PMID 38718135, Sci Transl Med 2024): single-dose autologous polyclonal expanded Tregs SAFE but DID NOT preserve residual beta-cell function over 12 months in 110 children with new-onset T1D vs placebo at high or low dose.; Important nuance: lower fold-expansion Tregs and an associated gene signature correlated with better C-peptide preservation, suggesting Treg QUALITY (not quantity / single-dose timing) may be the limiting factor.; Confirming activity: PolTREG PTG-007 (autologous Tregs) received positive EMA Paediatric Investigation Plan opinion May 2025; phase 2/3 readiness.; Engineered/antigen-specific Treg programs continuing (GNTI-122 in JCI Insight; CAR-Treg via Sonoma/Abata).; Status PARTIALLY_VALIDATED: hypothesis (Tregs alter T1D progression) is plausible and being trialed, but the only completed phase-2 RCT of polyclonal expanded Tregs was negative for the primary efficacy endpoint. Engineered approaches still uncertain.

rituximab -> T1D.validation_notes: Pescovitz NEJM 2009 + Diabetes Care 2014 2-yr extension: rituximab delays C-peptide loss ~8 mo but does not arrest beta-cell decline.

rituximab -> nephropathy.validation_notes: Path is a co-occurrence artifact from PMID 19940299 (Pescovitz NEJM 2009 — rituximab in new-onset T1D), where "diabetic nephropathy" is mentioned only as a T1D complication, NOT as a treatment indication for rituximab. Web validation 2026-05-03: rituximab is well-established for MEMBRANOUS NEPHROPATHY (PMID 35074299: meta-analysis of 11 trials, n=723, significant remission improvement) and other primary glomerular diseases (minimal change, lupus nephritis), but NOT for diabetic kidney disease. Multiple membranous nephropathy trials specifically EXCLUDE diabetic patients to avoid confounding. No RCT or systematic review evidence supports rituximab in diabetic nephropathy. RECOMMENDATION: drop this path from drug-repurposing dashboards or label explicitly as "membranous nephropathy (non-diabetic)" with a separate path. The rituximab -> T1D and rituximab -> beta_cell paths remain PARTIALLY_VALIDATED.

rituximab -> beta_cell.validation_notes: Pescovitz NEJM 2009 (PMID 19940299): single course of rituximab in new-onset T1D significantly preserved C-peptide AUC vs placebo at 12 months, lower HbA1c, less insulin. Pescovitz Diabetes Care 2014 2-yr follow-up (PMID 24026563): rate of C-peptide decline by 24-30 months parallels controls; cumulative effect = 8.2-month delay in beta-cell decline; effect wanes — does not arrest underlying autoimmunity. Beese BMC Medicine 2025 NMA (PMID 40598585): rituximab is among 11/42 interventions with significantly higher C-peptide at 12 months vs placebo, but ranks below teplizumab and low-dose ATG in cross-trial comparisons. Conclusion: rituximab partially preserves beta-cell function transiently but does not arrest beta-cell destruction. Effect is real but modest and time-limited. PARTIALLY_VALIDATED: same evidence base as rituximab -> T1D path.

teplizumab -> T1D.validation_notes: Teplizumab delays progression from Stage 2 to Stage 3 T1D by a median of ~2 years (Herold et al. NEJM 2019, PMID 31180194; TN-10 extended follow-up) and preserves C-peptide / reduces HbA1c in newly diagnosed T1D (PROTECT NEJM 2023, PMID 37865119). 2025-2026 real-world data replicate the signal: Diabetologia 2025 (DOI 10.1007/s00125-025-06646-6, 30 treated vs 10 controls), Mahesh et al. Diabetes Obesity & Metabolism 2026 (DOI 10.1111/dom.70354, only ~17% of 42 Stage 2 cases progressed to insulin in first year), and PMID 39949173 (2025 caregiver/adult real-world experiences). A meta-analysis of 8 RCTs (n=754) reports preserved C-peptide, reduced HbA1c, and insulin-initiation delay up to 24 months. Confidence HIGH.

teplizumab -> autoimmune.validation_notes: TN-10 (Herold et al. NEJM 2019, PMID 31180194): teplizumab 14-day course in stage 2 T1D relatives delayed median progression to stage 3 by ~24 months (HR 0.41); basis for 2022 FDA approval. PROTECT phase 3 (Ramos et al. NEJM 2023, PMID 37889505, n=328 stage 3 newly-diagnosed): stimulated C-peptide LSM difference +0.13 pmol/mL at week 78 (p<0.001), preserving beta cell function. VALIDATED. Cross-validated 2026-05-12.

SGLT2i_NLRP3_DKD.mechanism: SGLT2 inhibitors (dapagliflozin, empagliflozin) reduce NLRP3 inflammasome activation in renal tubular cells via (a) beta-hydroxybutyrate-induced NLRP3 inhibition, (b) accumulation of TCA-cycle immunometabolite itaconate, and (c) reduced RIP1-RIP3-MLKL-mediated necroinflammation, leading to decreased IL-1beta/IL-18/NLRP3 expression and attenuated renal fibrosis.
SGLT2i_NLRP3_DKD.clinical_anchor: Downstream kidney-outcome benefit of SGLT2i is established in large trials (CREDENCE, DAPA-CKD, EMPA-KIDNEY; see Lancet 2022 collaborative meta-analysis, PMID 36351458). NLRP3-axis remains the most parsimonious mechanistic explanation but has NOT been proven to mediate the clinical effect in humans.

BHB_to_NLRP3_inhibition.mechanism: β-hydroxybutyrate (BHB) inhibits NLRP3 inflammasome assembly by blocking K+ efflux and ASC oligomerization; independent of UCP2/Sirt2/Gpr109a/HDAC. SGLT2i raise serum BHB, providing a candidate mechanistic link to NLRP3 suppression in DKD/CV outcomes.

external_pmids.25686106: Youm et al. Nat Med 2015 — foundational: BHB blocks NLRP3-mediated disease (cell+mouse).
external_pmids.28794421: Yamanashi et al. Sci Rep 2017 — BHB endogenic NLRP3 inhibitor; anti-inflammatory in stress model.
external_pmids.32358544: Kim et al. Nat Commun 2020 — SGLT2i in T2D+CVD pts: ↑BHB, ↓insulin, ↓NLRP3-IL-1β in human macrophages (30-day RCT vs SU).
external_pmids.34918381: Front Pharmacol/Ke 2022 — already in library; SGLT2i↔NLRP3 via itaconate (alternate axis).
external_pmids.39412512: Braz J Nephrol 2024 — SGLT2i+NLRP3 in DKD review (already in library).

caveats: Most BHB→NLRP3 evidence is in vitro / mouse models. The in-human Kim 2020 study is a pharmacodynamic biomarker readout, not a clinical-outcome RCT.
BHB rise from SGLT2i is modest (typically 0.1–0.5 mmol/L) — whether this magnitude is sufficient to produce clinically meaningful NLRP3 inhibition in humans remains unproven.
2025 BMC Nephrology review (Springer; PMID not yet captured) and 2025 ADA abstract 389-P (BHB mitigates DKD) are non-PMID/abstract-only sources, so weight cautiously.
Alternative mechanisms (itaconate, RIP1-RIP3-MLKL, TXNIP-NLRP3) ALSO proposed for SGLT2i — BHB is not the sole or proven dominant axis.

PLOS One 2014 (PMC) reported NLRP3 not required for stress-induced islet death — controversy persists. Therefore PARTIALLY_VALIDATED, not VALIDATED.

verapamil_txnip_beta_cell_t1d.path_name: Verapamil -> TXNIP suppression -> beta cell preservation (T1D)
verapamil_txnip_beta_cell_t1d.rationale: Two independent RCTs confirm sustained C-peptide preservation. Ovalle 2018 (Nat Med, NCT02372253, n=24 completers, adults) showed verapamil improved MMTT-stimulated C-peptide AUC at both 3 and 12 months (prespecified primary endpoint), with lower insulin requirement increase and fewer hypoglycemic events. Forlenza CLVer trial 2023 (JAMA, n=88 pediatric ages 7-17) showed C-peptide 30% higher at 52 weeks vs placebo, with 95% vs 71% retaining peak C-peptide >=0.2 pmol/mL. Both trials used similar dosing and endpoint timing. Mechanism (TXNIP suppression) consistent with preclinical literature. AEs comparable to placebo.
verapamil_txnip_beta_cell_t1d.caveats: Both trials are short-term (12 months). The 2022 follow-up exploratory work (Nat Commun, Ovalle group) showed broader systemic effects but did not establish durability beyond 1 year. Ver-A-T1D protocol (PMC11605811) is a multicenter RCT still enrolling - longer-term durability and any disease-modification beyond C-peptide preservation remain open.

rituximab -> T1D.evidence: Pescovitz NEJM 2009 (PMID 19940299): RCT n=87, 4-dose rituximab vs placebo in newly diagnosed T1D. At 1 year, rituximab group had significantly higher C-peptide AUC, lower HbA1c, lower insulin requirements vs placebo. 2-year extension Pescovitz Diabetes Care 2014 (PMID 24026563): rate of C-peptide decline became parallel to placebo after ~8.2-month delay; effect transient. Conclusion: rituximab DELAYS but does not arrest beta-cell loss in recent-onset T1D. PARTIALLY_VALIDATED — real but limited durable benefit.
rituximab -> T1D.caveat: Effect plateaus by 30 months; no evidence of disease modification beyond delayed C-peptide loss. Underlying autoimmunity not arrested.

rituximab -> beta_cell.key_finding: Rituximab transiently preserves C-peptide (~8 mo delay in decline at 1-2 yr) but effect wanes; B-cell depletion alone insufficient to arrest beta-cell loss.

rituximab -> nephropathy (DIABETIC).key_finding: No clinical evidence supports rituximab for diabetic nephropathy. The path is a co-occurrence artifact. Rituximab IS validated for membranous nephropathy (PMID 35074299 meta-analysis), but that is a distinct, autoimmune-mediated glomerular disease — NOT diabetic kidney disease.

dapagliflozin_nephropathy.evidence_summary: DAPA-CKD landmark RCT (NEJM 2020 PMID 32970396, n=4304): dapagliflozin 10 mg vs placebo over median 2.4 y reduced composite (sustained ≥50% eGFR decline, ESKD, renal or CV death) HR 0.61 (95% CI 0.51-0.72). Confirmed by 2024 SR/MA (PMC11370938, 9 RCTs, ~30k participants) showing OR 0.61 (0.57-0.65) for primary kidney composite and OR 0.69 (0.63-0.76) for mortality, with UACR reduction of -23.99% (95% CI -34.82 to -13.15). Effect present in patients with and without T2D. Mechanism strongly supported.

dapagliflozin_T2D.evidence_summary: Landmark indication for dapagliflozin in T2D — VALIDATED. DECLARE-TIMI 58 (NEJM 2019, PMID 30415602; n=17,160 T2D patients, median 4.2 y follow-up): dapagliflozin 10 mg vs placebo MET non-inferiority for MACE (HR 0.93, 95% CI 0.84-1.03; p=0.17 for superiority) and was SUPERIOR for the co-primary composite of CV death/HF hospitalization (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.73-0.95; p=0.005), driven primarily by HF-hospitalization reduction (HR 0.73). Cardiorenal secondary composite (Mosenzon Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2019, PMID 31196815): HR 0.76 (0.67-0.87); renal-specific composite excluding CV death HR 0.53 (0.43-0.66). Effect consistent in patients with and without established CVD; benefit present in preserved-EF and reduced-EF subgroups. Multi-trial SGLT2i SR/MA (Zelniker Lancet 2019; updated 2024-2025 meta-analyses) places DECLARE alongside EMPA-REG, CANVAS, CREDENCE, EMPEROR, DAPA-HF, DAPA-CKD as collectively defining SGLT2i benefit in T2D for cardio-renal outcomes. ADA Standards of Care 2025 list dapagliflozin as guideline-recommended in T2D with established/at-risk CVD, HF, or CKD.
caveats: DAPA-HF and DAPA-CKD established benefit in patients without diabetes too — the dapagliflozin->T2D label has expanded into broader cardiorenal indications.

DECLARE was not powered for kidney hard endpoints (kidney-specific composite a secondary analysis); DAPA-CKD provides the dedicated kidney-outcome RCT (already validated separately as dapagliflozin_nephropathy).

verapamil_T1D.evidence_summary: Verapamil for adult newly-diagnosed T1D — PARTIALLY_VALIDATED with downgrade to MEDIUM after Ver-A-T1D EASD 2025 readout. Prior trials supporting beta-cell preservation: Ovalle 2018 Nat Med (PMID 29988125, n=24 completers, adults), positive at 12 mo; Forlenza CLVer 2023 JAMA (PMID 36826844, n=88 pediatric ages 7-17), C-peptide 30% higher at week 52 vs placebo (95% vs 71% retained peak C-peptide ≥0.2 pmol/mL). Ver-A-T1D (PMC11605811 protocol, EASD 2025 readout): n=136 adults across 21 sites in 6 European countries, slow-release verapamil 360 mg daily vs placebo for 12 months. RESULT: trend toward better C-peptide preservation in verapamil arm but DID NOT reach statistical significance — placebo decline (0.09 nmol/L/min) was lower than anticipated, reducing study power. No unexpected SAEs; some mild reversible cardiac AEs. Investigators conclude verapamil's effect in adults may be smaller than CLVer suggests for pediatric T1D, and recommend longer/larger combination trials. CLVer pediatric remains positive evidence; Ver-A-T1D adult signal is positive trend but underpowered/non-significant. Therefore PARTIALLY_VALIDATED, MEDIUM confidence (downgrade from earlier HIGH).
caveats: Ver-A-T1D 12-month adult readout did NOT reach statistical significance for C-peptide preservation (trend in favor of verapamil); cannot be cited as a positive RCT.
CLVer pediatric trial remains the strongest positive RCT; Ovalle 2018 is small (n=24 completers).
Future studies require larger samples, longer follow-up, and may need combination with immunomodulatory agents.
Underlying TXNIP-suppression mechanism remains plausible (verapamil_txnip_beta_cell_t1d entry covers preclinical chain).

Kidney disease progression or CV death 13.1% vs 16.9% (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.64-0.82, p<0.001) in CKD with or without diabetes (n=6,609).
Empagliflozin reduced composite CV death/HF hospitalization 25% in HFrEF; benefit extends to non-diabetic HF.

golimumab_t1d_beta_cell.caveats: Phase 2; not powered for long-term safety. No phase 3 confirmation. NMA reported substantial heterogeneity across 60 trials/42 interventions.
